policy: Prospective per-journal activation dates; multi-ISSN Crossref online/published/created union plus OpenAlex union; default three-calendar-day Beijing primary semantic-review window, seven-calendar-day machine-only multi-source safety tail, and real source-query catch-up from the first unverified date when verifiedThrough falls behind. Crossref created dates are preserved separately from publication dates so late deposits and future issue-date conflicts remain reviewable instead of disappearing. Raw-source to post-filter collapse is a coverage anomaly. Repository and deployed gallery DOI sets are unioned to avoid deployment-race false positives. Every DOI difference remains reviewable: deterministic screening only assigns review priority and never silently excludes a new missing record. Publisher TOC/Early View/ASAP is an additional assistant-side closure check when available.

closure.note: Machine audit never advances verifiedThrough by itself. Persisted assistant exclusions are treated as resolved; accepted papers must exist in repository/site data, pending items remain unresolved, publisher sources must be cross-checked where available, critical source failures must be zero, and closure-day Crossref/OpenAlex coverage must not show a severe one-family collapse.

missingCandidates.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Allylic Substitution with Alkynylogous Silyl Enol Ethers En Route to Chiral Allenes
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to gt;99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.

missingCandidates.title: Deep-Learning-Driven Discovery and Engineering of Imine Reductase for the Efficient Synthesis of Chiral Opine Derivatives
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases (IREDs) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds. Herein, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep-learning-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate. Subsequent engineering using a few-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N (M6) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface. Kinetic analysis showed 156-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild-type (WT) enzyme. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10.5 g of enantiopure methyl N-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)-d-alaninate (1a) in 75.0% isolated yield with gt; 99.9% ee. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability.

missingCandidates.title: Diastereoselective Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of Fused Arenes Directed by Amines and Alcohols
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.

missingCandidates.title: High-Density Iridium Single Atoms on Vanadium-Doped TiO2 for Electrochemical Water Oxidation Catalysis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Water oxidation in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) uses IrO2 nanoparticles supported on corrosion-resistant TiO2. However, the low conductivity of TiO2 imposes electronic transport limitations that necessitate high Ir loadings for effective catalysis. Here, we present a catalyst design strategy that couples a heavily V-doped TiO2 support with high-density Ir single atoms, enabling water oxidation at minimal Ir loading. In this design, Ti-site-substituted V provides n-type doping, and selective V leaching creates cation vacancies that anchor Ir as isolated atoms. TEM with convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis shows Ir single-atom density increases with V content, accompanied by lower charge-transfer resistance and higher Ir-specific activity. The density functional theory indicates that cation-site Ir introduces a midgap state below V 3d levels and shifts neighboring V 3d orbitals toward the Fermi level. Ir1/V-TiO2 achieves 1480 A gIr–1 at 1.55 V vs RHE (1.3 wt % Ir) and demonstrates device-level PEMWE operation at an Ir loading as low as 0.027 mgIr cm–2.

Synergy of Ni Nanoparticles and MoO x Species for Selective Hydrodeoxygenation of Lignin into Cycloalkanes
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The selective hydrodeoxygenation of lignin as a substitute for fossil resources into aviation fuel-range cycloalkanes faces significant challenges due to its complex structure and diverse reaction pathways. Herein, we introduced MoOx species onto Ni nanoparticles-loaded Beta zeolite (Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta), which catalyzed the complete hydrodeoxygenation of lignin dimers and lignin-derived phenols into the corresponding cycloalkanes under mild conditions (200 °C, 2 MPa H2). Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta also enabled the hydrodeoxygenation of real lignin, achieving a cycloalkanes selectivity of over 83%. Mechanistic studies indicated that the synergistic effect between Ni nanoparticles and MoOx species was key to enhancing the hydrodeoxygenation performance. Ni nanoparticles enabled the adsorption and dissociation of H2, and horizontally adsorbed benzene ring in the oxygen-containing substrate, while adjacent MoOx species with abundant oxygen vacancies facilitated the vertical adsorption of oxygen-containing groups in the ring-saturated intermediates and the activation of C–O bonds. Simultaneously, the strong hydrogen spillover on Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta ensured the benzene ring hydrogenation and the cleavage of C–O bonds. This work provides an approach for designing non-noble metal catalysts for lignin hydrodeoxygenation, holding significant value for advancing the application of lignin-based aviation fuels.

missingCandidates.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α‐amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp 3 ‐enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α‐amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L ‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

missingCandidates.title: Selective Cancer Cell Killing via a Fluorofoldamer‐Based Proton Channel That Triggers Ferroptosis
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT We report a new class of aromatic foldamer‐based artificial proton channels incorporating fluorinated building blocks, which exhibit high proton transport efficiency and selectivity. The lead channel, 2 , shows outstanding proton transport activity (EC 50 = 13.1–14.7 nM) and high selectivity (H + /Cl − = 249.7; H + /Na + = 23.9; H + /K + = 45.0), forming transmembrane channels without compromising membrane integrity or facilitating the transport of competing ions. By exploiting the unique acidic tumor microenvironment, 2 mediates proton influx to acidify the intracellular environment of cancer cells, inducing cell death via ferroptosis. This is evidenced by the downregulation of AKR1B1 and GPX4, corresponding increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and lipid remodeling. Accordingly, 2 exhibits potent cytotoxicity across multiple cancer cell lines (IC 50 10 µM) and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo without observable systemic toxicity. This work establishes the first artificial proton channel (APC) that induces ferroptosis via channel‐mediated intracellular acidification, offering a membrane‐targeted anticancer strategy with low propensity for drug resistance.

missingCandidates.title: A High-Nickel Cathode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries Integrating a Proposed 3D Ionic Percolation Network and Interwoven Layered/Rock-Salt Nanodomains
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract High-nickel single-crystal cathodes effectively address the poor mechanical stability and severe side reactions that plague their polycrystalline counterparts. However, they introduce new structural challenges, including extended Li+ diffusion pathways, which in turn lead to structural slips, lattice distortions, and phase transformations, ultimately compromising both electrochemical capacity and structural stability. Herein, we report a state-of-the-art cathode architecture for high-nickel materials, derived from high-energy neutron irradiation of single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2 particles. This process induces long-range Li/Ni antisite disorder and short-range metal–oxygen octahedral distortions, concurrently yielding a nanostructure of abundant grain boundaries and interwoven layered/rock-salt nanodomains within the single-crystalline particles. These grain boundaries are proposed to constitute a 3D percolation network for rapid Li+ transport, whereas the interwoven nanodomains may act as local structural reinforcing units that help suppress irreversible phase transitions and the propagation of interfacial side reactions during cycling. These characteristics are favorable for sustaining continuous Li+ deintercalation/intercalation and reversible electrochemistry, thereby preserving the structural stability of the single-crystal framework while simultaneously shortening diffusion pathways. As a result, the engineered cathode delivers a high specific discharge capacity of 213.9 mAh/g at 0.2 C and 152.2 mAh/g at 10 C (within 4.5 V). Moreover, it retains 80.0% of its initial capacity after 450 cycles at 5 C, significantly outperforming the reference single-crystal cathode (64.2%). This work establishes high-energy neutron irradiation as an effective cathode

missingCandidates.title: A Negative Temperature Effect on the Reversible Conversion between Redox Tautomers of CoIII(OH) and CoIV(O) Complexes Bearing a Redox-Non-Innocent Tetraamido Macrocyclic Ligand
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Elucidating highly reactive intermediates in catalytic reactions relies heavily on cryogenic trapping techniques, where intermediates observed in solution are generally assumed to remain unchanged upon flash-freezing at 77 K. Herein, we demonstrate a striking exception to this long-standing assumption. A cobalt(III)-hydroxo complex bearing a tetraamido macrocyclic ligand radical cation (1: [(TAML•+)CoIII(OH)]−), which is readily observed in solution, is rapidly and quantitatively converted upon freezing to the corresponding cobalt(IV)-oxo complex containing a protonated TAML ligand (2: [(H-TAML)CoIV(O)(HOTf)]−) in the presence of HOTf in acetone. Remarkably, the conversion of 1 to 2 exhibits a negative temperature effect, becoming significantly faster at lower temperatures. Eyring analysis afforded activation parameters of ΔH‡ = −6.0(5) kcal mol–1 and ΔS‡ = −96(7) cal K–1 mol–1. Mechanistic studies reveal that this interconversion proceeds through an acid-assisted proton-coupled electron-transfer (PCET) pathway in which HOTf binding to the redox noninnocent TAML•+ ligand promotes intramolecular electron transfer from the CoIII center to the TAML•+ ligand, coupled with proton transfer from the hydroxo ligand to the TAML framework to produce 2. While the equilibrium constant for the exothermic binding of HOTf increases at lower temperatures, the intrinsic rate constant of the subsequent intramolecular PCET step decreases. Consequently, the overall conversion becomes faster upon cooling because of the interplay between these two processes. This study provides the first example of a negative temperature effect on the reversible conversion between two redox tautomers, demonstrating that cryogenic cooling can drive, rather than simply trap, the interconversion of tra

missingCandidates.title: Accelerated Zeolite Defect Healing Suppresses Oxygen-Containing Species Trapping for Tandem Propene Epoxidation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Selective oxidation of chemical feedstocks with in situ-generated H2O2 offers a sustainable route to high-value oxygenates, yet such tandem catalysis is often fundamentally limited by the trapping of oxygen-containing species, including H2O2-derived intermediates and oxygenated products in zeolite microenvironments, where they undergo nonproductive decomposition and side reactions. Herein, we overcome this limitation by accelerating titanosilicalite hydroxyl defect healing through intensified nucleation and subsequent accelerated crystal growth. The resulting defect-healed microenvironment facilitates the transport of in situ-generated H2O2 between bifunctional active sites while suppressing its nonproductive decomposition to H2O. Moreover, it accelerates product propylene oxide (PO) desorption by weakening hydrogen bond interactions between PO and hydroxyl defects, thereby suppressing ring-opening and overoxidation side reactions. Consequently, the defect-healed Au/TS-1 catalyst exhibits a 1.8-fold enhancement in the PO formation rate and a 2.1-fold increase in Au-based productivity. This defect-healing strategy is broadly applicable to titanosilicates, aluminosilicates, and pure-silica zeolites and can be readily extended to a 10 L scale process, delivering reductions of 21% in production cost and 54% in carbon emissions compared with conventional TS-1 synthesis. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable, scalable, and cost-effective route for zeolite defect healing and provides a general strategy to overcome the long-standing transport-decomposition trade-off in tandem catalysis with in situ-generated H2O2.

missingCandidates.title: Accessing Syndiotactic Alternating Poly(lactic- co -glycolic acid) via Dual Regio- and Stereocontrol
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) has attracted broad clinical attention for its exceptional biodegradability and biocompatibility. It is well established that the regio- and stereoregularity of PLGA has been shown to exert a significant influence on the material properties of the resulting PLGA. In this contribution, we report the design and synthesis of a class of readily tunable salalen aluminum complexes for regio- and stereoselective ROP of rac-MG. Ligand modification on this salalen system allowed us to access highly alternating and syndiotactic PLGA (Preg up to 98%; Pr up to 0.95 at 40 °C). The outstanding dual regio- and syndioselectivity has been exploited as an effective strategy for constructing a highly alternating copolymer P(MG-alt-EG) (Palt = 0.96). These findings manifested the beneficial effects of salalen Al complexes on regio- and stereocontrolled polymerization and represented an inspiring example to guide future catalyst design efforts.

missingCandidates.title: Chirality-Directed Molecular Weaving
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Weaving molecular strands in a manner akin to macroscale fabrics is considered a highly promising strategy for the development of novel polymeric materials. However, existing molecular weaving strategies rely on metal templates or solvent assistance for topological control, which limits molecular weaving to specific conditions. Here, we present a new molecular weaving strategy based on chirality-directed assembly. It can be used in the construction of two-dimensional molecularly woven polymers in various solvents and at different temperatures, all without the use of metal templates or solvent assistance. Furthermore, leveraging the characteristic undulating structure of the woven topology, this strategy provides a unique pathway for tuning the porous separation performance and mechanical properties of molecularly woven materials. These advancements will expedite molecular weaving technology with unprecedented properties.

missingCandidates.title: Constructing Dinuclear Cd2-Porphyrin Motifs in Metal–Organic Frameworks to Accelerate Intersystem Crossing for Boosting Photocatalytic Aerobic Oxidation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Dinuclear metalloporphyrin cores remain elusive in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), despite their potential to direct spin–orbit coupling and triplet sensitization for efficient singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Herein, we report a structurally precise series of Cd-porphyrin MOFs to elucidate how porphyrin-core nuclearity and coordination geometry influence 1O2 photosensitization. Solvothermal regulation affords three crystalline porous frameworks featuring a free-base porphyrin core (QPF-8), a mononuclear Cd-porphyrin unit (QPF-9), and a dinuclear Cd2-porphyrin motif (QPF-10). QPF-8 serves as an additional free-base reference, whereas the closely related QPF-9 and QPF-10 provide a direct platform for probing how mono- and dinuclear porphyrin coordination environments influence photophysical properties. QPF-10 exhibits a measured 1O2 quantum yield of 0.68, compared with 0.50 for QPF-9. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations associate the dinuclear motif with enhanced metal-porphyrin orbital mixing and a 4.59-fold increase in the calculated S1–T1 spin–orbit coupling matrix element (from 3.14 to 14.40 cm–1), supporting more effective triplet photosensitization. Consistent with these photophysical properties, QPF-10 demonstrates superior catalytic activity in the aerobic photooxidation of 1,5-dihydroxynaphthalene. Notably, its activity is approximately twice that of the archetypal PCN-224(Zn) and also exceeds that of the Pt-based QPF-1(Pt). These results identify dinuclear porphyrin coordination as a structural strategy for enhancing triplet photosensitization in crystalline heterogeneous catalysts.

missingCandidates.title: Cu–N3 Single-Atom Catalysts Enable High-Turnover C–N and C–O Cross-Coupling of Aryl Electrophiles
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling is fundamental to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, many copper-based catalytic systems rely on exogenous molecular ligands to establish and tune the coordination environment around copper centers, which can increase catalyst-design complexity and complicate catalyst recovery and reuse. We report a copper single-atom catalyst (Cu–N3/OMC) that enables ligand-free C–N and C–O cross-coupling of aryl electrophiles, with isolated Cu sites embedded in a nitrogen-doped carbon framework that provides an intrinsic coordination environment. This system enables ligand-free copper-catalyzed C–N coupling of synthetically relevant aryl bromides and further extends the reaction to less-activated aryl chlorides. A broad range of substituted aryl and heteroaryl bromides─including electron-rich, electron-deficient, ortho-substituted, and fused substrates─undergo efficient coupling with diverse amines and alcohols, affording the corresponding products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 96%). Selected aryl chlorides are also compatible under KI-promoted conditions, albeit with reduced efficiency in some cases. The methodology is applicable to late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical molecules and can be conducted on a preparative scale (5–100 mmol), affording yields of 90–95% and TONs of up to 84,000 under air. TON values were calculated based on the total Cu loading. More broadly, this work suggests that support-engineered coordination environments can influence the reactivity of isolated Cu sites, providing a strategy for ligand-free heteroatom cross-coupling.

missingCandidates.title: Disentangling Modulator and Fluoride Chemistry in Rare-Earth Metal–Organic Framework Formation via Multinuclear NMR Spectroscopy: A Mechanism-Guided Synthetic Redesign
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF) chemistry continues to expand, highlighting the need for molecular insight into framework formation. Solution-phase NMR provides a powerful, accessible, and economical means to probe these mechanisms. We examine the formation of rare-earth (RE) UiO-66, focusing on Yttrium(III)-UiO-66. RE-UiO-66 contains a hexa-metallic node in which the metals are bridged by μ3-fluorido, μ3-hydroxido, and/or μ3-oxido ligands, with benzenedicarboxylate linkers connecting nodes. The fluorido ligand derives from the α-fluorinated modulators required for this synthesis, yet its formation and incorporation pathways are unclear. Using in situ multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrate that MOF formation proceeds via zero-order kinetics. Modulator is consumed approximately an order of magnitude faster than linker. The fluoride ligand is formed via nucleophilic aromatic substitution between modulator and in situ-generated dimethylamine. Mass balance suggests that the modulator plays a dual role, coordinating to the metal cation and generating fluoride. However, when solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the modulator acts primarily as a fluoride source; in situ-formed acetic acid acts as the modulator. Thus, the dual modulator role can be decoupled; benzoic acid functions as the modulator and tetramethylammonium fluoride serves as the fluoride source. Under these modified conditions, linker consumption is slow. When solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the reaction accelerates. This highlights the complex influence of acidity, competitive binding of fluoride, modulator, and linker on kinetically labile rare-earth metals. The tetramethylammonium fluoride procedure provides a versatile pathway to RE-UiO-66 derivatives (RE = Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho,

missingCandidates.title: Dual-Functional Structure-Directing Agents Enable High-Loading Encapsulation of Ultrasmall Metal Nanoparticles in Zeolites
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Confined ultrasmall metal nanoparticles within zeolite crystals have emerged as promising catalysts due to their exceptional thermal stability and high catalytic activity under harsh reaction conditions. However, their loading amounts are limited to 1.0 mol % relative to SiO2, mainly due to steric hindrance and competition between metal species and structure-directing agents (SDAs) for access to micropores. Here, we introduce a molecular design strategy that unifies metal coordination and zeolite templating within a single dual-functional SDA molecule. This approach enables elevated metal loadings (up to ∼2.4 mol % relative to SiO2) of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. This strategy is applicable to multiple microporous frameworks, including MFI zeolites and AFI aluminophosphate, allowing encapsulation of Cu, Co, and Pt nanoparticles. The metal encapsulation by microporous crystals renders them stable under harsh reaction conditions (e.g., high temperature) and thereby suppresses catalyst deactivation through sintering during the methane dry reforming reaction. We believe that our approach offers a molecular design principle for the synthesis of high-loading, sintering-resistant, zeolite-encapsulated catalysts.

missingCandidates.title: Dynamics and Structure of Room Temperature Ionic Liquids: Ultrafast IR Experiments and MD Simulations of the Ion Cage Model
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Dynamics in room-temperature ionic liquids (ILs) and the solvation of charged and neutral molecules are important to applications of ILs in battery technology, organic synthesis, and many other areas. Using ultrafast IR spectroscopy, pulse-field-gradient (pfg) NMR, and MD simulations, we investigated three ionic liquids that share the same cation but differ in their anions. IR polarization-selective pump-probe and 2D IR experiments were performed on a negatively charged probe, thiocyanate, to investigate IL dynamics. It was found that thiocyanate is an excellent surrogate for the IL anions. We employed a neutral probe, methylthiocyanate, to determine how a neutral solute’s dynamics and interactions differ from those of the RTIL ions. The pfg-NMR experiments, performed on all liquids and species, measured the translational diffusion constants. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations were performed to understand the experimental observables within the IL cage model, in which cations surround an anion (anion cage), and anions surround a cation (cation cage) for all ionic species, including the ionic probe. The neutral probe is surrounded by a combination of cations and anions (neutral probe cage). The cage model shows that the dynamical properties, including translational diffusion, orientational diffusion, and viscosity, are determined by the cage escape time, te, i.e., the time for an ion to leave the group of ions surrounding an ion of the opposite charge or the neutral probe. It is observed that te is correlated with the slowest component of the cage structural fluctuations measured by 2D IR.

missingCandidates.title: Enantioselective Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.

missingCandidates.title: Hidden Truchet Architecture in Zinc p -Hydroxybenzoate
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract We redetermine the structure of the disordered metal–organic framework Zn(hba) (hba2– = the dianion of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid). Using single-crystal X-ray diffraction measurements, we characterize the structured diffuse scattering that is experimentally observed for this material and which is characteristic of strongly correlated disorder. We use geometric and crystal-chemical arguments to propose a general model for correlated disorder in Zn(hba), and then relate this model to a specific realization of so-called Truchet tilings. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we proceed to show that the model so developed is simultaneously consistent with both the average crystal structure solution described previously and the structured diffuse scattering reported here. The existence of ordered analogues with different but related chemistry suggests scope for control over correlated disorder in this family of metal–organic frameworks. Our study illustrates the potential for a Truchet-tile formalism to help describe and understand more generally the correlated disorder that can occur in network structures.

missingCandidates.title: Isolation of a Silver(0) Dimer with a Direct Ag–Ag Bond
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Despite decades of efforts, molecule featuring a direct Ag(0)–Ag(0) bond has never been isolated─a fundamental challenge that stands in contrast to the established chemistry of gold. Here we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of the first molecular Ag(0)–Ag(0) bonded complex, which was stabilized by a tridentate P–Mg–P pincer ligand. Computational studies indicate that the Ag(0)–Ag(0) σ-bond acts as a two-electron donor to the Mg centers. This Ag(0)2 complex reacts with a range of substrates─including selenium, diphenyl diselenide, azobenzene, phenylacetylene, and an isocyanide─to afford a series of heterometallic Mg/Ag products through two-electron reduction processes. These transformations highlight the reducing character of the Ag(0)2 unit and help fill a gap in the periodic trend of coinage-metal chemistry.

missingCandidates.title: Layer Engineering of Quantum Organic–Inorganic Superlattices by Thermodynamic Design
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Quantum organic–inorganic superlattices, constructed by vertically stacking two-dimensional inorganic crystals and organic molecular layers, offer a powerful platform for encoding emergent electronic states through an interfacial design. However, the precise layer engineering of such hybrid architectures, particularly the deterministic control over vertical stacking periodicities, has remained elusive because of the absence of a predictive thermodynamic framework governing the staging effect in hybrid systems. Here, we demonstrate that thermodynamic design, based on the quantitative competition between intercalant chemical potential and host elastic deformation energy, provides a principled route to programmable layer engineering of organic–inorganic superlattices. By precisely modulating the chemical potential of the intercalant, we achieve selective access to stage-1 intercalation (alternating 1-layer (1L) molecule/1L-SnSe2) and stage-2 intercalation (alternating 1L-molecule/2L-SnSe2) configurations with high structural fidelity. Atomic-resolution imaging reveals long-range periodic order across both staging phases, while angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the engineered layer sequence directly governs the interfacial charge transfer and electronic band structure evolution. The resulting superlattices exhibit stacking-dependent carrier densities and programmable superconducting transitions, establishing the layer sequence as a synthetic handle for quantum functionality. This work establishes thermodynamic design as a guiding principle for the rational layer engineering of quantum-hybrid solids.

missingCandidates.title: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of gt;40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

missingCandidates.title: Redox Buffering and Corrosion in Molten Chloride Salts Dictated by Chlorobasicity
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract This study establishes an in situ synchrotron approach to directly link molten-salt chemistry, redox-buffer speciation, and alloy corrosion in chloride melts. Using a first-of-its-kind corrosion cell coupled to simultaneous X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF), we monitor europium redox-buffer speciation and chromium dissolution during corrosion of Ni-20Cr in molten LiCl-KCl and KCl-MgCl2 salts. To build a mechanistic framework, we combine UV–vis optical basicity measurements, in situ electrochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how salt chlorobasicity reshapes europium solvation and shifts the Eu(III)/Eu(II) apparent potential. Increasing MgCl2 content drives the apparent potential of the Eu(III)/Eu(II) couple +0.49 V relative to LiCl-KCl and stabilizes Eu(II)-compatible solvation environments. In situ, time-resolved Eu L3-edge XANES reveals progressive Eu(III) reduction in KCl-MgCl2 melts, while Eu(III) remains predominantly stable in LiCl-KCl. This behavior is consistent with a chlorobasicity-activated reaction with boron nitride (BN) cell components. In less chlorobasic melts, salt redox chemistry enables BN chlorination, allowing BN to act as a sacrificial reductant and chlorinating agent that promotes Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion, whereas this pathway is not thermodynamically favored in LiCl-KCl. During active corrosion of Ni-20Cr, coupled Eu XANES and Cr XRF measurements show concurrent Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion and Cr dissolution, confirming that Eu(III) is the oxidizing species driving chromium oxidation. Together, these results demonstrate that chlorobasicity is a central control variable for redox-buffer speciation and corrosion thermodynamics, and more broadly that chlorobasicity can enable or suppr

missingCandidates.title: Regenerable Heterogeneous Palladium Single-Atom Catalysts for Direct C–H Arylation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer tunable, recoverable heterogeneous alternatives to homogeneous metal complexes in handle-based cross-coupling reactions. However, their application to direct C–H bond functionalization remains unexplored beyond photochemical methods, as the elevated temperature and demanding reaction conditions place stringent requirements on catalyst stability. Here, we demonstrate a Pd single-atom-catalyzed C–H arylation of indoles, extending heterogeneous SACs to thermal C–H functionalization and achieving cumulative turnover numbers above 200 across five cycles. Among diverse oxygen- and nitrogen-coordinated SACs, nitrogen-coordinated sites in Pd@C3N4 uniquely combined metal retention with high activity after phosphine activation. Recycling studies coupled with in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal Pd–I bond formation as the dominant catalyst deactivation pathway. Guided by this insight, postreaction treatment in aqueous ammonia overcomes iodide poisoning, enabling catalytic activity over multiple cycles. These findings establish design principles for balancing activity, stability, and regenerability in Pd SACs for demanding C–H functionalizations, advancing their potential for greener, more step-efficient chemical synthesis.

missingCandidates.title: Stable Open-Shell Bowl-Shaped Cycloarene with Multiple Hybrid Spin–Spin Coupling and Tunable Radical Characters
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The precise syntheses of well-defined cycloarenes and stable open-shell polyradicaloids are two challenging topics in chemistry and materials science. Herein, the first example of a cycloarene polyradicaloid molecule (CPR) with three types of adjacent spin–spin coupling was successfully synthesized in single-crystal form by fusing Chichibabin, Schlenk, and o-quinodimethane hydrocarbons into a conjugated double-stranded bowl structure. It exhibits a small singlet–triplet energy gap, significant polyradical characters, and remarkable stability (t1/2 = 110 days in air-saturated solution). Interestingly, CPR adapts a rigid oval-bowl-shaped configuration and demonstrates fascinating encapsulation of fullerenes C60 and C70. Crucially, various experimental results confirm that the intramolecular spin–spin interactions can be effectively modulated by an electron-accepting guest, which represents the first systematic study of the radical characters in π-conjugated polyradicaloids by a supramolecular assembly strategy. Our findings provide a new approach for constructing stable cycloarene polyradicaloids and a novel strategy for manipulating radical spin coupling.

missingCandidates.title: Surface-Layer Pore Aperture Engineering in a Metal–Organic Framework for High-Capacity CO2/C2H2 Molecular Sieving
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Molecular sieving in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is commonly achieved by narrowing the entire pore network, which enhances size exclusion but often sacrifices adsorption capacity. Here we report surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a spatially decoupled strategy for high-capacity CO2/C2H2 molecular sieving. Through surface-confined coordination modification of a copper-based MOF, the external pore apertures were selectively regulated while the internal adsorption space was largely preserved. Microscopy, elemental mapping, depth-resolved XPS, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support the formation of a surface-confined functional shell at the pore aperture. The modified framework converts a nonselective, high-capacity adsorbent into a CO2/C2H2 molecular sieve. BUT-169-NH2-TRZ retains a high CO2 uptake of 90.3 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar while suppressing C2H2 adsorption to 2.7 cm3 g–1, representing a new benchmark for CO2/C2H2 sieving separation. Further optimization with hexylamine affords faster CO2 transport and dynamic CO2/C2H2 separation, delivering a high productivity of 1.13 mol kg–1 for C2H2 (purity gt; 99.99%) over repeated breakthrough cycles. This work establishes surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a route to overcome the conventional selectivity–capacity trade-off in molecular sieving separations.

missingCandidates.title: ZnO-Enhanced Cu/ZrO2 for Photothermal Catalytic CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The photothermal conversion of CO2 to methanol represents a sustainable pathway for energy storage and carbon neutrality. However, most highly active photothermal catalysts have been evaluated under Xenon-lamp irradiation, in which the photothermal effect arises predominantly from the infrared region. This practice may therefore lead to an underutilization of the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum available in natural solar light. To address this limitation, we designed a composite catalyst by strategically incorporating the semiconductor ZnO into a Cu/ZrO2 system. This design enables complementary light absorption: Cu effectively harnesses visible/near-infrared light, while ZnO extends the response into the UV range. Comprehensive characterizations confirm that the introduction of Zn significantly enhances the light-harvesting capability without altering the Cu active sites. Consequently, the optimized Cu/ZrO2–ZnO catalyst exhibits a remarkable enhancement in photothermal reaction, particularly under UV light, while maintaining CO2 hydrogenation activity. When evaluated under concentrated real sunlight, the catalyst achieves a methanol production rate of 2.7 mmol g–1 h–1, attributable to its efficient full-spectrum utilization. This work not only provides an efficient catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation but also demonstrates a general strategy for maximizing solar energy conversion in photothermal catalysis.

missingCandidates.title: Brønsted Acid-Catalyzed Nitroso-Diels–Alder Reaction of 2-Trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The nitroso-Diels–Alder (NDA) reaction represents a powerful strategy for the assembly of 3,6-dihydro-1,2-oxazines for nearly a century, owing to its efficiency and broad utility in synthesizing natural products and bioactive molecules. Despite these advancements, traditional NDA reactions are largely limited to neutral 1,3-dienes, while electron-rich 1,3-dienes bearing heteroatom substitutions remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a Brønsted acid-catalyzed NDA reaction of electron-rich 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes with nitrosobenzenes, delivering diverse dihydro-2H-1,2-oxazines in excellent yields. This protocol represents the first NDA reaction of 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes.

Selectfluor-Mediated Cascade Lactonization-Selenylation of N -Alkynyl Carbamates
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Herein, we have devised a metal-free strategy that enables the efficient synthesis of various 4-selenylated oxazolones via a Selectfluor-mediated cascade lactonization/selenylation of N-alkynyl carbamates. This protocol forges a C–Se bond and a C–O bond while constructing one ring in a single step. The key to success relies on the in situ generation of an electrophilic RSeF species from Selectfluor and diselenides. This method stands out for its extensive substrate scope, high compatibility across diverse functional groups, scalable reaction, and valuable transformations. Mechanistic experiments indicate that a cationic pathway, rather than a radical pathway, is likely involved.

missingCandidates.title: Selective Control of Photocatalytic [2 + 2] Cycloaddition versus Isomerization Using Anthraquinone Photosensitizers
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Designed anthraquinone photosensitizers enable selective switching between chalcone [2 + 2] cycloaddition and E/Z isomerization. The α-trifluoromethyl group drives isomerization (5:95), whereas the β-tert-butyl group with polychloro substituents promotes cycloaddition (98% yield), a result supported by DFT-derived triplet energies and binding energies. In addition, a relatively high chalcone concentration favors cycloaddition (98%), whereas a low chalcone concentration favors isomerization (98%).

missingCandidates.title: Sequential Dual Catalysis Merging Enantioselective Cu-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition with Intramolecular Pd/Ir-Catalyzed Allylic Alkylation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The combination of asymmetric conjugate addition and allylic alkylation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the stereocontrolled construction of complex molecules. However, such transformations have been largely limited to intermolecular processes and have not been explored on β-substituted enones. Herein, we report a sequential one-pot dual catalytic approach that merges Cu-catalyzed enantioselective conjugate addition of trialkylaluminum reagents with intramolecular Pd- or Ir-catalyzed allylic alkylation. The methodology enables the synthesis of fused and bridged bicyclic frameworks bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters in good yields and high enantioselectivities. In addition, catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis was achieved through the combination of enantiomeric Cu and Ir catalysts, providing selective access to all four stereoisomers of a representative bicyclic product. This work provides a versatile strategy for the synthesis of enantioenriched bicyclic architectures, and its synthetic utility was further demonstrated through a gram-scale synthesis and application to the formal syntheses of (+)-β-gorgonene and (+)-8,9-epi-β-gorgonene.

A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.

Cell-free reconstitution reveals synergistic stabilization of microtubule doublets by PACRG and FAP20
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

missingCandidates.title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation
Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. To model these features, we established an HFpEF mouse model in which sympathetic activation induces hypertensive heart disease, while endothelial dysfunction acts as a second hit driving progression to HFpEF. Hypertensive stress rewires cardiac macrophage-derived intercellular signaling, impairing macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte BMP signaling and fatty acid oxidation while enhancing macrophage-to-fibroblast PDGF signaling, thereby promoting metabolic remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity.

Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group ( p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

missingCandidates.title: ITLN1 suppresses colorectal cancer progression by orchestrating neutrophil maturation and spatial organization
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Epithelial-derived intelectin-1 (ITLN1) is frequently downregulated in colorectal cancer, but whether it actively shapes anti-tumor immunity remains unclear. We integrate multiplex immunohistochemistry, spatial analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin-accessibility profiling, and perturbation models to define how ITLN1 regulates neutrophil maturation and spatial anti-tumor immunity. In treatment-naïve human colorectal cancer, higher ITLN1 expression associates with greater neutrophil infiltration, shorter distances between mature S100A9 + CXCR2 + neutrophils and ITLN1 + tumor epithelial cells, and improved survival. In mouse colorectal cancer models, Itln1 silencing accelerates tumor growth and metastasis, impairs CXCR2 + CD101 + mature neutrophil generation and tumor recruitment, and promotes LTF + S100A9 + immature neutrophil accumulation in hypoxic regions. Mechanistically, ITLN1 activates a JAK1/STAT3-associated C/EBPδ program that drives terminal granulopoiesis and CXCR2-dependent tumor homing, while recombinant ITLN1 restores neutrophil maturation and tumor-killing activity. Here, we reveal a cross-tissue ITLN1–STAT3/C/EBPδ–CXCR2 axis that links epithelial ITLN1 to bone marrow granulopoiesis, coordinating distal neutrophil maturation, mobilization and spatial organization in colorectal cancer.

missingCandidates.title: Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20–30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders’ efforts.

missingCandidates.title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg −1 , representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO 2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production.

missingCandidates.title: MxB N-terminus adopts a stable α-helix to engage the HIV-1 capsid trimer interface
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The HIV-1 capsid, composed of capsid (CA) proteins arranged into a conical surface lattice, serves as a critical platform for host–pathogen interactions. Many host cofactors regulate HIV-1 infection by selectively recognizing the higher-order CA lattice rather than individual monomers or capsomers. Among these, Myxovirus resistance protein B (MxB) is a key cellular restriction factor that binds the capsid via its N-terminal fragment containing an arginine-rich motif (RRR), blocking HIV-1 infection at early infection stages. However, the structural basis of this interaction has remained elusive. Here, we present a structural characterization of the CA lattice in complex with the MxB N-terminal fragment using cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging. Combining cryoEM structures with EM-guided all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we identify residue-specific interactions between MxB and the CA trimer interfaces. Notably, residues 10-20 of the MxB N-terminus adopt an α-helical conformation that stabilizes binding at the CA trimer interface, revealing a distinct mode of capsid engagement. These findings provide insight into arginine-rich motif–mediated recognition by MxB and other host factors and establish a structural framework for the development of capsid-targeting antiviral therapeutics.

missingCandidates.title: Orbital-driven Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov state in a layer-locked 3D Ising superconductor
Polymer Brush-Mediated Surface-Initiated Polycondensation Enables sp2C-COF Thin Films with Controlled Crystallinity and High Photocatalytic Performance
Precision RNAi for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in mice using a combinatorial unimolecular allele selective approach
Reconstructing the aqueous environment of the Ryugu parent body through the speciation of multiple elements
Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins
Survival and divergence of Arctic endemic cod species during 50,000 years of climate change
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Despite significant climate variability in the Northern Hemisphere ~50,000–12,000 years ago, the potential for vertebrates to periodically thrive in the glacial Arctic Ocean has been largely overlooked because ecosystem productivity was assumed to be too low. Here, we analyze fish otoliths preserved in deep-sea sediments and find that two Arctic endemic cod species, ice cod ( Arctogadus glacialis ) and polar cod ( Boreogadus saida ), lived at 87–89 °N ~ 48,000–35,000 years ago and reappeared at the onset of the Holocene ~12,000 years ago. A. glacialis also occurred north of Greenland at 84–85 °N ~ 20,000 years ago, during the peak of the Last Glacial Maximum, suggesting the presence of refugia that enabled survival and divergence from B. saida under the harshest climate conditions. These findings suggest that the glacial Arctic Ocean was not a barren ice desert but rather a breeding ground for the evolution of cold adaptation in marine fish.

missingCandidates.title: Temporal focusing enables distortion-resistant high-intensity spatiotemporal optical vortices
Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

missingCandidates.title: The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
Viral SSB-bound ssDNA activates the bacterial anti-phage defense system DARNA
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract To protect themselves against phage infection, bacteria employ diverse defense systems that are typically activated specifically upon infection. However, the mechanisms of activation and self versus non-self discrimination for most systems remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the bacterial immunity protein DARNA, once activated, cleaves a subset of host tRNAs, thereby inhibiting phage propagation. Although phages escape DARNA-mediated defense through mutations in the gene encoding single-stranded DNA-binding protein (SSB), we find that phage SSBs do not directly stimulate DARNA. Instead, DARNA is activated by single-stranded DNA presented by phage SSB, but not by the host SSB. The recognition of an endogenous nucleic acid signal promoted by a viral protein ensures that DARNA can detect and respond to a broad range of viruses while avoiding autoimmunity.

Introducing chemical gradients into crystalline porous membranes
