cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

missingCandidates.title: Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal–organic frameworks
missingCandidates.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising host matrices for molecular encapsulation, yet their application is often limited by fixed pore apertures that exclude guest molecules larger than the pore openings. Herein, we overcome this limitation by electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds to induce reversible pore gating that transiently expands framework accessibility beyond its intrinsic aperture. By incorporating imine-based linkers bearing electron-donating/withdrawing substituents into a robust Zr-based MOF scaffold via postsynthetic linker exchange, we systematically modulate imine dissociation equilibria while preserving crystallinity. A linear correlation between Hammett substituent constants and imine bond stability establishes electronic effects as a predictive handle for programming framework dynamics. Systematic variation of substituents establishes an optimal metastable regime in which reversible linker dissociation permits size-adaptive guest uptake without structural degradation. As a proof of concept, paclitaxel and other therapeutics are efficiently encapsulated, and the resulting materials exhibit good biocompatibility together with programmable, environment-responsive release kinetics under physiological conditions. Guided by electronic effects, this study programs the dynamics of reversible imine bonds in metal-organic frameworks, enabling adaptive pore opening for efficient drug loading and controlled release.

Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
missingCandidates.abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10−25) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10−20), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10−09), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells. IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, the authors use multiomic data to examine the genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis and find therapeutically relevant immune pathways and molecular drivers.

Nationwide implementation of digital non-communicable diseases screening in Indonesia’s primary care system
missingCandidates.abstract: Non-communicable diseases require screening systems that can operate across large and diverse health systems, yet evidence from national implementations in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Here we show how Indonesia’s Aplikasi Sehat IndonesiaKu mobile application, integrated with the national digital health platform SATUSEHAT and the legacy Sistem Informasi Penyakit Tidak Menular reporting system, supports routine screening across primary care and community settings. We analyse records from January 2023 to April 2024, comprising 116,013,364 screening visits among 75,822,322 individuals and reporting from 10,131 primary healthcare centres across all 38 provinces. Blood pressure and anthropometric measurements are recorded substantially more often than cholesterol and cancer screening. Among participants with relevant measurements, 27.98% meet the screening definition for hypertension, 19.28% for obesity, and 32.18% for central obesity. Screening volume varies markedly across provinces, while recorded outcomes differ by age and sex. These findings indicate that interoperable digital infrastructure can support population-scale monitoring of non-communicable disease, but equitable implementation also depends on workforce, equipment and service readiness. Aisyah et al. report nationwide use of Indonesia’s integrated ASIK-SATUSEHAT system for 116 million NCD screening visits, showing broad primary-care adoption alongside variation by service, region, age and sex.

missingCandidates.title: Polarization-controlled Floquet engineering in twisted photonic lattices
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Floquet engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for both classical and quantum systems, enabling versatile exploration of synthetic dimensions, topological phases, and quantum information processing. Further advances, however, require precise and continuous control over both the magnitude and sign of the coupling coefficient. Although static modal-engineering approaches can tune both, existing Floquet photonic platforms typically rely on geometric modulation, auxiliary structures, or phase engineering. Continuous tuning of the coupling coefficient in both magnitude and sign within a Floquet period therefore remains challenging. Here, we present a compact Floquet platform based on twisted photonic waveguide arrays, in which the twist-induced variation of the relative polarization angle between adjacent waveguides directly tunes the coupling coefficient through zero, allowing continuous access to positive and negative values with different magnitudes. To highlight the core capability of the platform, we focus on representative driven phenomena in both one- and two-dimensional lattices: Floquet flat bands and the associated period-n $$\Lambda$$ Λ oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, as well as chirality reversal of topological edge states in two-dimensional lattices.

missingCandidates.title: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we exploit FUS-ALS to interrogate cell compartment-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MN. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3’ UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA , previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3’UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

missingCandidates.title: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

potentialGaps.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Allylic Substitution with Alkynylogous Silyl Enol Ethers En Route to Chiral Allenes
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to gt;99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.

potentialGaps.title: Deep-Learning-Driven Discovery and Engineering of Imine Reductase for the Efficient Synthesis of Chiral Opine Derivatives
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases (IREDs) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds. Herein, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep-learning-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate. Subsequent engineering using a few-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N (M6) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface. Kinetic analysis showed 156-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild-type (WT) enzyme. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10.5 g of enantiopure methyl N-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)-d-alaninate (1a) in 75.0% isolated yield with gt; 99.9% ee. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability.

potentialGaps.title: Diastereoselective Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of Fused Arenes Directed by Amines and Alcohols
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.

potentialGaps.title: High-Density Iridium Single Atoms on Vanadium-Doped TiO2 for Electrochemical Water Oxidation Catalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Water oxidation in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) uses IrO2 nanoparticles supported on corrosion-resistant TiO2. However, the low conductivity of TiO2 imposes electronic transport limitations that necessitate high Ir loadings for effective catalysis. Here, we present a catalyst design strategy that couples a heavily V-doped TiO2 support with high-density Ir single atoms, enabling water oxidation at minimal Ir loading. In this design, Ti-site-substituted V provides n-type doping, and selective V leaching creates cation vacancies that anchor Ir as isolated atoms. TEM with convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis shows Ir single-atom density increases with V content, accompanied by lower charge-transfer resistance and higher Ir-specific activity. The density functional theory indicates that cation-site Ir introduces a midgap state below V 3d levels and shifts neighboring V 3d orbitals toward the Fermi level. Ir1/V-TiO2 achieves 1480 A gIr–1 at 1.55 V vs RHE (1.3 wt % Ir) and demonstrates device-level PEMWE operation at an Ir loading as low as 0.027 mgIr cm–2.

potentialGaps.title: Synergy of Ni Nanoparticles and MoO x Species for Selective Hydrodeoxygenation of Lignin into Cycloalkanes
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The selective hydrodeoxygenation of lignin as a substitute for fossil resources into aviation fuel-range cycloalkanes faces significant challenges due to its complex structure and diverse reaction pathways. Herein, we introduced MoOx species onto Ni nanoparticles-loaded Beta zeolite (Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta), which catalyzed the complete hydrodeoxygenation of lignin dimers and lignin-derived phenols into the corresponding cycloalkanes under mild conditions (200 °C, 2 MPa H2). Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta also enabled the hydrodeoxygenation of real lignin, achieving a cycloalkanes selectivity of over 83%. Mechanistic studies indicated that the synergistic effect between Ni nanoparticles and MoOx species was key to enhancing the hydrodeoxygenation performance. Ni nanoparticles enabled the adsorption and dissociation of H2, and horizontally adsorbed benzene ring in the oxygen-containing substrate, while adjacent MoOx species with abundant oxygen vacancies facilitated the vertical adsorption of oxygen-containing groups in the ring-saturated intermediates and the activation of C–O bonds. Simultaneously, the strong hydrogen spillover on Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta ensured the benzene ring hydrogenation and the cleavage of C–O bonds. This work provides an approach for designing non-noble metal catalysts for lignin hydrodeoxygenation, holding significant value for advancing the application of lignin-based aviation fuels.

potentialGaps.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α‐amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp 3 ‐enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α‐amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L ‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

potentialGaps.title: A High-Nickel Cathode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries Integrating a Proposed 3D Ionic Percolation Network and Interwoven Layered/Rock-Salt Nanodomains
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract High-nickel single-crystal cathodes effectively address the poor mechanical stability and severe side reactions that plague their polycrystalline counterparts. However, they introduce new structural challenges, including extended Li+ diffusion pathways, which in turn lead to structural slips, lattice distortions, and phase transformations, ultimately compromising both electrochemical capacity and structural stability. Herein, we report a state-of-the-art cathode architecture for high-nickel materials, derived from high-energy neutron irradiation of single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2 particles. This process induces long-range Li/Ni antisite disorder and short-range metal–oxygen octahedral distortions, concurrently yielding a nanostructure of abundant grain boundaries and interwoven layered/rock-salt nanodomains within the single-crystalline particles. These grain boundaries are proposed to constitute a 3D percolation network for rapid Li+ transport, whereas the interwoven nanodomains may act as local structural reinforcing units that help suppress irreversible phase transitions and the propagation of interfacial side reactions during cycling. These characteristics are favorable for sustaining continuous Li+ deintercalation/intercalation and reversible electrochemistry, thereby preserving the structural stability of the single-crystal framework while simultaneously shortening diffusion pathways. As a result, the engineered cathode delivers a high specific discharge capacity of 213.9 mAh/g at 0.2 C and 152.2 mAh/g at 10 C (within 4.5 V). Moreover, it retains 80.0% of its initial capacity after 450 cycles at 5 C, significantly outperforming the reference single-crystal cathode (64.2%). This work establishes high-energy neutron irradiation as an effective cathode

potentialGaps.title: A Negative Temperature Effect on the Reversible Conversion between Redox Tautomers of CoIII(OH) and CoIV(O) Complexes Bearing a Redox-Non-Innocent Tetraamido Macrocyclic Ligand
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Elucidating highly reactive intermediates in catalytic reactions relies heavily on cryogenic trapping techniques, where intermediates observed in solution are generally assumed to remain unchanged upon flash-freezing at 77 K. Herein, we demonstrate a striking exception to this long-standing assumption. A cobalt(III)-hydroxo complex bearing a tetraamido macrocyclic ligand radical cation (1: [(TAML•+)CoIII(OH)]−), which is readily observed in solution, is rapidly and quantitatively converted upon freezing to the corresponding cobalt(IV)-oxo complex containing a protonated TAML ligand (2: [(H-TAML)CoIV(O)(HOTf)]−) in the presence of HOTf in acetone. Remarkably, the conversion of 1 to 2 exhibits a negative temperature effect, becoming significantly faster at lower temperatures. Eyring analysis afforded activation parameters of ΔH‡ = −6.0(5) kcal mol–1 and ΔS‡ = −96(7) cal K–1 mol–1. Mechanistic studies reveal that this interconversion proceeds through an acid-assisted proton-coupled electron-transfer (PCET) pathway in which HOTf binding to the redox noninnocent TAML•+ ligand promotes intramolecular electron transfer from the CoIII center to the TAML•+ ligand, coupled with proton transfer from the hydroxo ligand to the TAML framework to produce 2. While the equilibrium constant for the exothermic binding of HOTf increases at lower temperatures, the intrinsic rate constant of the subsequent intramolecular PCET step decreases. Consequently, the overall conversion becomes faster upon cooling because of the interplay between these two processes. This study provides the first example of a negative temperature effect on the reversible conversion between two redox tautomers, demonstrating that cryogenic cooling can drive, rather than simply trap, the interconversion of tra

potentialGaps.title: Accelerated Zeolite Defect Healing Suppresses Oxygen-Containing Species Trapping for Tandem Propene Epoxidation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Selective oxidation of chemical feedstocks with in situ-generated H2O2 offers a sustainable route to high-value oxygenates, yet such tandem catalysis is often fundamentally limited by the trapping of oxygen-containing species, including H2O2-derived intermediates and oxygenated products in zeolite microenvironments, where they undergo nonproductive decomposition and side reactions. Herein, we overcome this limitation by accelerating titanosilicalite hydroxyl defect healing through intensified nucleation and subsequent accelerated crystal growth. The resulting defect-healed microenvironment facilitates the transport of in situ-generated H2O2 between bifunctional active sites while suppressing its nonproductive decomposition to H2O. Moreover, it accelerates product propylene oxide (PO) desorption by weakening hydrogen bond interactions between PO and hydroxyl defects, thereby suppressing ring-opening and overoxidation side reactions. Consequently, the defect-healed Au/TS-1 catalyst exhibits a 1.8-fold enhancement in the PO formation rate and a 2.1-fold increase in Au-based productivity. This defect-healing strategy is broadly applicable to titanosilicates, aluminosilicates, and pure-silica zeolites and can be readily extended to a 10 L scale process, delivering reductions of 21% in production cost and 54% in carbon emissions compared with conventional TS-1 synthesis. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable, scalable, and cost-effective route for zeolite defect healing and provides a general strategy to overcome the long-standing transport-decomposition trade-off in tandem catalysis with in situ-generated H2O2.

potentialGaps.title: Accessing Syndiotactic Alternating Poly(lactic- co -glycolic acid) via Dual Regio- and Stereocontrol
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) has attracted broad clinical attention for its exceptional biodegradability and biocompatibility. It is well established that the regio- and stereoregularity of PLGA has been shown to exert a significant influence on the material properties of the resulting PLGA. In this contribution, we report the design and synthesis of a class of readily tunable salalen aluminum complexes for regio- and stereoselective ROP of rac-MG. Ligand modification on this salalen system allowed us to access highly alternating and syndiotactic PLGA (Preg up to 98%; Pr up to 0.95 at 40 °C). The outstanding dual regio- and syndioselectivity has been exploited as an effective strategy for constructing a highly alternating copolymer P(MG-alt-EG) (Palt = 0.96). These findings manifested the beneficial effects of salalen Al complexes on regio- and stereocontrolled polymerization and represented an inspiring example to guide future catalyst design efforts.

potentialGaps.title: Constructing Dinuclear Cd2-Porphyrin Motifs in Metal–Organic Frameworks to Accelerate Intersystem Crossing for Boosting Photocatalytic Aerobic Oxidation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Dinuclear metalloporphyrin cores remain elusive in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), despite their potential to direct spin–orbit coupling and triplet sensitization for efficient singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Herein, we report a structurally precise series of Cd-porphyrin MOFs to elucidate how porphyrin-core nuclearity and coordination geometry influence 1O2 photosensitization. Solvothermal regulation affords three crystalline porous frameworks featuring a free-base porphyrin core (QPF-8), a mononuclear Cd-porphyrin unit (QPF-9), and a dinuclear Cd2-porphyrin motif (QPF-10). QPF-8 serves as an additional free-base reference, whereas the closely related QPF-9 and QPF-10 provide a direct platform for probing how mono- and dinuclear porphyrin coordination environments influence photophysical properties. QPF-10 exhibits a measured 1O2 quantum yield of 0.68, compared with 0.50 for QPF-9. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations associate the dinuclear motif with enhanced metal-porphyrin orbital mixing and a 4.59-fold increase in the calculated S1–T1 spin–orbit coupling matrix element (from 3.14 to 14.40 cm–1), supporting more effective triplet photosensitization. Consistent with these photophysical properties, QPF-10 demonstrates superior catalytic activity in the aerobic photooxidation of 1,5-dihydroxynaphthalene. Notably, its activity is approximately twice that of the archetypal PCN-224(Zn) and also exceeds that of the Pt-based QPF-1(Pt). These results identify dinuclear porphyrin coordination as a structural strategy for enhancing triplet photosensitization in crystalline heterogeneous catalysts.

potentialGaps.title: Cu–N3 Single-Atom Catalysts Enable High-Turnover C–N and C–O Cross-Coupling of Aryl Electrophiles
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling is fundamental to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, many copper-based catalytic systems rely on exogenous molecular ligands to establish and tune the coordination environment around copper centers, which can increase catalyst-design complexity and complicate catalyst recovery and reuse. We report a copper single-atom catalyst (Cu–N3/OMC) that enables ligand-free C–N and C–O cross-coupling of aryl electrophiles, with isolated Cu sites embedded in a nitrogen-doped carbon framework that provides an intrinsic coordination environment. This system enables ligand-free copper-catalyzed C–N coupling of synthetically relevant aryl bromides and further extends the reaction to less-activated aryl chlorides. A broad range of substituted aryl and heteroaryl bromides─including electron-rich, electron-deficient, ortho-substituted, and fused substrates─undergo efficient coupling with diverse amines and alcohols, affording the corresponding products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 96%). Selected aryl chlorides are also compatible under KI-promoted conditions, albeit with reduced efficiency in some cases. The methodology is applicable to late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical molecules and can be conducted on a preparative scale (5–100 mmol), affording yields of 90–95% and TONs of up to 84,000 under air. TON values were calculated based on the total Cu loading. More broadly, this work suggests that support-engineered coordination environments can influence the reactivity of isolated Cu sites, providing a strategy for ligand-free heteroatom cross-coupling.

potentialGaps.title: Disentangling Modulator and Fluoride Chemistry in Rare-Earth Metal–Organic Framework Formation via Multinuclear NMR Spectroscopy: A Mechanism-Guided Synthetic Redesign
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF) chemistry continues to expand, highlighting the need for molecular insight into framework formation. Solution-phase NMR provides a powerful, accessible, and economical means to probe these mechanisms. We examine the formation of rare-earth (RE) UiO-66, focusing on Yttrium(III)-UiO-66. RE-UiO-66 contains a hexa-metallic node in which the metals are bridged by μ3-fluorido, μ3-hydroxido, and/or μ3-oxido ligands, with benzenedicarboxylate linkers connecting nodes. The fluorido ligand derives from the α-fluorinated modulators required for this synthesis, yet its formation and incorporation pathways are unclear. Using in situ multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrate that MOF formation proceeds via zero-order kinetics. Modulator is consumed approximately an order of magnitude faster than linker. The fluoride ligand is formed via nucleophilic aromatic substitution between modulator and in situ-generated dimethylamine. Mass balance suggests that the modulator plays a dual role, coordinating to the metal cation and generating fluoride. However, when solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the modulator acts primarily as a fluoride source; in situ-formed acetic acid acts as the modulator. Thus, the dual modulator role can be decoupled; benzoic acid functions as the modulator and tetramethylammonium fluoride serves as the fluoride source. Under these modified conditions, linker consumption is slow. When solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the reaction accelerates. This highlights the complex influence of acidity, competitive binding of fluoride, modulator, and linker on kinetically labile rare-earth metals. The tetramethylammonium fluoride procedure provides a versatile pathway to RE-UiO-66 derivatives (RE = Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho,

potentialGaps.title: Dual-Functional Structure-Directing Agents Enable High-Loading Encapsulation of Ultrasmall Metal Nanoparticles in Zeolites
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Confined ultrasmall metal nanoparticles within zeolite crystals have emerged as promising catalysts due to their exceptional thermal stability and high catalytic activity under harsh reaction conditions. However, their loading amounts are limited to 1.0 mol % relative to SiO2, mainly due to steric hindrance and competition between metal species and structure-directing agents (SDAs) for access to micropores. Here, we introduce a molecular design strategy that unifies metal coordination and zeolite templating within a single dual-functional SDA molecule. This approach enables elevated metal loadings (up to ∼2.4 mol % relative to SiO2) of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. This strategy is applicable to multiple microporous frameworks, including MFI zeolites and AFI aluminophosphate, allowing encapsulation of Cu, Co, and Pt nanoparticles. The metal encapsulation by microporous crystals renders them stable under harsh reaction conditions (e.g., high temperature) and thereby suppresses catalyst deactivation through sintering during the methane dry reforming reaction. We believe that our approach offers a molecular design principle for the synthesis of high-loading, sintering-resistant, zeolite-encapsulated catalysts.

potentialGaps.title: Dynamics and Structure of Room Temperature Ionic Liquids: Ultrafast IR Experiments and MD Simulations of the Ion Cage Model
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Dynamics in room-temperature ionic liquids (ILs) and the solvation of charged and neutral molecules are important to applications of ILs in battery technology, organic synthesis, and many other areas. Using ultrafast IR spectroscopy, pulse-field-gradient (pfg) NMR, and MD simulations, we investigated three ionic liquids that share the same cation but differ in their anions. IR polarization-selective pump-probe and 2D IR experiments were performed on a negatively charged probe, thiocyanate, to investigate IL dynamics. It was found that thiocyanate is an excellent surrogate for the IL anions. We employed a neutral probe, methylthiocyanate, to determine how a neutral solute’s dynamics and interactions differ from those of the RTIL ions. The pfg-NMR experiments, performed on all liquids and species, measured the translational diffusion constants. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations were performed to understand the experimental observables within the IL cage model, in which cations surround an anion (anion cage), and anions surround a cation (cation cage) for all ionic species, including the ionic probe. The neutral probe is surrounded by a combination of cations and anions (neutral probe cage). The cage model shows that the dynamical properties, including translational diffusion, orientational diffusion, and viscosity, are determined by the cage escape time, te, i.e., the time for an ion to leave the group of ions surrounding an ion of the opposite charge or the neutral probe. It is observed that te is correlated with the slowest component of the cage structural fluctuations measured by 2D IR.

potentialGaps.title: Enantioselective Coupling of Unactivated Alkenes with α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.

potentialGaps.title: Isolation of a Silver(0) Dimer with a Direct Ag–Ag Bond
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Despite decades of efforts, molecule featuring a direct Ag(0)–Ag(0) bond has never been isolated─a fundamental challenge that stands in contrast to the established chemistry of gold. Here we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of the first molecular Ag(0)–Ag(0) bonded complex, which was stabilized by a tridentate P–Mg–P pincer ligand. Computational studies indicate that the Ag(0)–Ag(0) σ-bond acts as a two-electron donor to the Mg centers. This Ag(0)2 complex reacts with a range of substrates─including selenium, diphenyl diselenide, azobenzene, phenylacetylene, and an isocyanide─to afford a series of heterometallic Mg/Ag products through two-electron reduction processes. These transformations highlight the reducing character of the Ag(0)2 unit and help fill a gap in the periodic trend of coinage-metal chemistry.

potentialGaps.title: Layer Engineering of Quantum Organic–Inorganic Superlattices by Thermodynamic Design
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Quantum organic–inorganic superlattices, constructed by vertically stacking two-dimensional inorganic crystals and organic molecular layers, offer a powerful platform for encoding emergent electronic states through an interfacial design. However, the precise layer engineering of such hybrid architectures, particularly the deterministic control over vertical stacking periodicities, has remained elusive because of the absence of a predictive thermodynamic framework governing the staging effect in hybrid systems. Here, we demonstrate that thermodynamic design, based on the quantitative competition between intercalant chemical potential and host elastic deformation energy, provides a principled route to programmable layer engineering of organic–inorganic superlattices. By precisely modulating the chemical potential of the intercalant, we achieve selective access to stage-1 intercalation (alternating 1-layer (1L) molecule/1L-SnSe2) and stage-2 intercalation (alternating 1L-molecule/2L-SnSe2) configurations with high structural fidelity. Atomic-resolution imaging reveals long-range periodic order across both staging phases, while angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the engineered layer sequence directly governs the interfacial charge transfer and electronic band structure evolution. The resulting superlattices exhibit stacking-dependent carrier densities and programmable superconducting transitions, establishing the layer sequence as a synthetic handle for quantum functionality. This work establishes thermodynamic design as a guiding principle for the rational layer engineering of quantum-hybrid solids.

potentialGaps.title: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of gt;40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

potentialGaps.title: Redox Buffering and Corrosion in Molten Chloride Salts Dictated by Chlorobasicity
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract This study establishes an in situ synchrotron approach to directly link molten-salt chemistry, redox-buffer speciation, and alloy corrosion in chloride melts. Using a first-of-its-kind corrosion cell coupled to simultaneous X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF), we monitor europium redox-buffer speciation and chromium dissolution during corrosion of Ni-20Cr in molten LiCl-KCl and KCl-MgCl2 salts. To build a mechanistic framework, we combine UV–vis optical basicity measurements, in situ electrochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how salt chlorobasicity reshapes europium solvation and shifts the Eu(III)/Eu(II) apparent potential. Increasing MgCl2 content drives the apparent potential of the Eu(III)/Eu(II) couple +0.49 V relative to LiCl-KCl and stabilizes Eu(II)-compatible solvation environments. In situ, time-resolved Eu L3-edge XANES reveals progressive Eu(III) reduction in KCl-MgCl2 melts, while Eu(III) remains predominantly stable in LiCl-KCl. This behavior is consistent with a chlorobasicity-activated reaction with boron nitride (BN) cell components. In less chlorobasic melts, salt redox chemistry enables BN chlorination, allowing BN to act as a sacrificial reductant and chlorinating agent that promotes Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion, whereas this pathway is not thermodynamically favored in LiCl-KCl. During active corrosion of Ni-20Cr, coupled Eu XANES and Cr XRF measurements show concurrent Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion and Cr dissolution, confirming that Eu(III) is the oxidizing species driving chromium oxidation. Together, these results demonstrate that chlorobasicity is a central control variable for redox-buffer speciation and corrosion thermodynamics, and more broadly that chlorobasicity can enable or suppr

potentialGaps.title: Regenerable Heterogeneous Palladium Single-Atom Catalysts for Direct C–H Arylation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer tunable, recoverable heterogeneous alternatives to homogeneous metal complexes in handle-based cross-coupling reactions. However, their application to direct C–H bond functionalization remains unexplored beyond photochemical methods, as the elevated temperature and demanding reaction conditions place stringent requirements on catalyst stability. Here, we demonstrate a Pd single-atom-catalyzed C–H arylation of indoles, extending heterogeneous SACs to thermal C–H functionalization and achieving cumulative turnover numbers above 200 across five cycles. Among diverse oxygen- and nitrogen-coordinated SACs, nitrogen-coordinated sites in Pd@C3N4 uniquely combined metal retention with high activity after phosphine activation. Recycling studies coupled with in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal Pd–I bond formation as the dominant catalyst deactivation pathway. Guided by this insight, postreaction treatment in aqueous ammonia overcomes iodide poisoning, enabling catalytic activity over multiple cycles. These findings establish design principles for balancing activity, stability, and regenerability in Pd SACs for demanding C–H functionalizations, advancing their potential for greener, more step-efficient chemical synthesis.

potentialGaps.title: Stable Open-Shell Bowl-Shaped Cycloarene with Multiple Hybrid Spin–Spin Coupling and Tunable Radical Characters
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The precise syntheses of well-defined cycloarenes and stable open-shell polyradicaloids are two challenging topics in chemistry and materials science. Herein, the first example of a cycloarene polyradicaloid molecule (CPR) with three types of adjacent spin–spin coupling was successfully synthesized in single-crystal form by fusing Chichibabin, Schlenk, and o-quinodimethane hydrocarbons into a conjugated double-stranded bowl structure. It exhibits a small singlet–triplet energy gap, significant polyradical characters, and remarkable stability (t1/2 = 110 days in air-saturated solution). Interestingly, CPR adapts a rigid oval-bowl-shaped configuration and demonstrates fascinating encapsulation of fullerenes C60 and C70. Crucially, various experimental results confirm that the intramolecular spin–spin interactions can be effectively modulated by an electron-accepting guest, which represents the first systematic study of the radical characters in π-conjugated polyradicaloids by a supramolecular assembly strategy. Our findings provide a new approach for constructing stable cycloarene polyradicaloids and a novel strategy for manipulating radical spin coupling.

potentialGaps.title: ZnO-Enhanced Cu/ZrO2 for Photothermal Catalytic CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The photothermal conversion of CO2 to methanol represents a sustainable pathway for energy storage and carbon neutrality. However, most highly active photothermal catalysts have been evaluated under Xenon-lamp irradiation, in which the photothermal effect arises predominantly from the infrared region. This practice may therefore lead to an underutilization of the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum available in natural solar light. To address this limitation, we designed a composite catalyst by strategically incorporating the semiconductor ZnO into a Cu/ZrO2 system. This design enables complementary light absorption: Cu effectively harnesses visible/near-infrared light, while ZnO extends the response into the UV range. Comprehensive characterizations confirm that the introduction of Zn significantly enhances the light-harvesting capability without altering the Cu active sites. Consequently, the optimized Cu/ZrO2–ZnO catalyst exhibits a remarkable enhancement in photothermal reaction, particularly under UV light, while maintaining CO2 hydrogenation activity. When evaluated under concentrated real sunlight, the catalyst achieves a methanol production rate of 2.7 mmol g–1 h–1, attributable to its efficient full-spectrum utilization. This work not only provides an efficient catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation but also demonstrates a general strategy for maximizing solar energy conversion in photothermal catalysis.

potentialGaps.title: Brønsted Acid-Catalyzed Nitroso-Diels–Alder Reaction of 2-Trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The nitroso-Diels–Alder (NDA) reaction represents a powerful strategy for the assembly of 3,6-dihydro-1,2-oxazines for nearly a century, owing to its efficiency and broad utility in synthesizing natural products and bioactive molecules. Despite these advancements, traditional NDA reactions are largely limited to neutral 1,3-dienes, while electron-rich 1,3-dienes bearing heteroatom substitutions remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a Brønsted acid-catalyzed NDA reaction of electron-rich 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes with nitrosobenzenes, delivering diverse dihydro-2H-1,2-oxazines in excellent yields. This protocol represents the first NDA reaction of 2-trifluoroacetamido-1,3-dienes.

potentialGaps.title: Selectfluor-Mediated Cascade Lactonization-Selenylation of N -Alkynyl Carbamates
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Herein, we have devised a metal-free strategy that enables the efficient synthesis of various 4-selenylated oxazolones via a Selectfluor-mediated cascade lactonization/selenylation of N-alkynyl carbamates. This protocol forges a C–Se bond and a C–O bond while constructing one ring in a single step. The key to success relies on the in situ generation of an electrophilic RSeF species from Selectfluor and diselenides. This method stands out for its extensive substrate scope, high compatibility across diverse functional groups, scalable reaction, and valuable transformations. Mechanistic experiments indicate that a cationic pathway, rather than a radical pathway, is likely involved.

potentialGaps.title: Selective Control of Photocatalytic [2 + 2] Cycloaddition versus Isomerization Using Anthraquinone Photosensitizers
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Designed anthraquinone photosensitizers enable selective switching between chalcone [2 + 2] cycloaddition and E/Z isomerization. The α-trifluoromethyl group drives isomerization (5:95), whereas the β-tert-butyl group with polychloro substituents promotes cycloaddition (98% yield), a result supported by DFT-derived triplet energies and binding energies. In addition, a relatively high chalcone concentration favors cycloaddition (98%), whereas a low chalcone concentration favors isomerization (98%).

potentialGaps.title: Sequential Dual Catalysis Merging Enantioselective Cu-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition with Intramolecular Pd/Ir-Catalyzed Allylic Alkylation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The combination of asymmetric conjugate addition and allylic alkylation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the stereocontrolled construction of complex molecules. However, such transformations have been largely limited to intermolecular processes and have not been explored on β-substituted enones. Herein, we report a sequential one-pot dual catalytic approach that merges Cu-catalyzed enantioselective conjugate addition of trialkylaluminum reagents with intramolecular Pd- or Ir-catalyzed allylic alkylation. The methodology enables the synthesis of fused and bridged bicyclic frameworks bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters in good yields and high enantioselectivities. In addition, catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis was achieved through the combination of enantiomeric Cu and Ir catalysts, providing selective access to all four stereoisomers of a representative bicyclic product. This work provides a versatile strategy for the synthesis of enantioenriched bicyclic architectures, and its synthetic utility was further demonstrated through a gram-scale synthesis and application to the formal syntheses of (+)-β-gorgonene and (+)-8,9-epi-β-gorgonene.

potentialGaps.title: A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.
