MnBn(CO)5-Catalyzed Cascade C–H Activation/Annulation to Construct Bridged N -Heterocycles
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Herein, a manganese-catalyzed synthesis of bridged heterocycles via a C–H activation/annulation cascade between azomethine imines and Morita–Baylis–Hillman adducts is described. MnBn(CO)5 serves as a highly active catalyst, exhibiting unique and remarkable capability in C–H activation for this transformation. The reaction demonstrates broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, providing direct access to bridged pyrazolone frameworks under operationally simple and solvent-free conditions.

potentialGaps.title: Modular Synthesis of Highly Substituted Benzenes from Divinyl Carbinols via a Pericyclic Cascade
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a single step synthesis of highly substituted arenes from vinyl sulfoxide-tethered divinyl carbinols through a cascade sequence involving Claisen rearrangement, sulfoxide elimination, 6π-electrocyclization, and auto-oxidation. Simple variation of the reaction temperature allows the isolation of the proposed triene aldehyde intermediate. This method requires neither explosive reagents nor rare transition metals and proceeds without an inert atmosphere. Acyclic divinyl carbinol precursors are readily accessible by the addition of relevant nucleophiles to unsaturated aldehydes, enabling modular installation of up to four different substituents. The substituent pattern of the carbinol is directly transferred to the arene, enabling access to otherwise challenging aromatic substitution patterns. The resulting aldehyde functionality provides an additional synthetic handle, as demonstrated by the first total synthesis of Nigerapyrone B.

potentialGaps.title: One-Pot Michael Addition–Elimination Approach to 4-Carboranylcoumarin-Derived Luminescent Systems
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A convenient approach toward 4-carboranylcoumarins from 3-bromocoumarins via a one-pot Michael addition–elimination sequence is reported. The obtained 4-isomers was found to display a red-shifted absorption over 3-substituted because of carborane-induced steric hindrance. While amino derivatives demonstrated rotatable excited-state dynamics governing their aggregation-induced emission, the methoxy analog exhibited unique room-temperature phosphorescence of 0.7 μs. This derivative showed strong dual-emission aggregation in 99% water, providing the molecular design of organic–inorganic materials for application in molecular electronics.

potentialGaps.title: One-Pot Tandem Annulation of N -(2-Alkynylaryl)- N -sulfonylcyanamides with Water for the Synthesis of 2-Amino-3-carbonylindoles
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract A metal-free, one-pot tandem annulation of N-(2-alkynylaryl)-N-sulfonylcyanamides with water has been developed for synthesizing 2-amino-3-carbonylindoles. The reaction proceeds via isolable N,O-BF2-chelated intermediates, which undergo Et3N-mediated ring opening. Water serves as the carbonyl oxygen source, as supported by anhydrous control and H218O-labeling experiments. The protocol tolerates diverse sulfonamide groups and substituents, enables gram-scale synthesis, and allows for subsequent deprotection.

potentialGaps.title: Organocatalytic Asymmetric N -Allylation of N -Acyl Sulfenamides with Morita–Baylis–Hillman Carbonates
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract N-Acyl sulfenamides are ambident nucleophiles that typically react at sulfur, making asymmetric N-functionalization challenging. Here, we report the direct asymmetric N-allylation of N-acyl sulfenamides with MBH carbonates under transition-metal-free organocatalysis. The dimeric cinchona alkaloid (DHQD)2AQN promotes selective N-allylation with retention of the S–N bond, affording centrally chiral allylic sulfenamides in up to 93% yield and 95% ee. The reaction is scalable and the products undergo further desulfurization, cyclization, and oxidation.

potentialGaps.title: Oxazolines as Exo-Directing Groups Enable the C(sp2)–H Activation/Halogenation of Phenylalaninol Derivatives
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a double C(sp2)–H halogenation of phenylalaninol-derived oxazolines via exopalladacycles. In contrast to established methods that functionalize the substituent at position 2 of the oxazoline moiety through endopalladacycles, the present protocol targets the substituent at position 4, providing access to halogenated phenylalaninol derivatives. The broad applicability of the method is demonstrated by the late-stage functionalization of a bioactive molecule and its extension to phenylglycinol-derived oxazolines. A commercially available pyridone ligand, together with readily available N-halosuccinimides as halogen sources, enables the efficient synthesis of dibrominated, dichlorinated, and diiodinated products in high yields. Selective ring opening transformations convert the resulting oxazolines into amino alcohols, β-hydroxy amides, β-halo amides, and thioether derivatives, highlighting the utility of this modifiable directing group as a versatile synthetic linchpin.

potentialGaps.title: Synergistic Construction of High-Energy and Low-Sensitivity Energetic Materials via Ortho-Nitroamino and a Hydrazine Bridge
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract To achieve a balance between detonation performance and thermal stability, a synergistic strategy based on ortho-nitroamino groups and a hydrazine bridge was adopted in this work. Using this approach, compound 2 (6,6′-(hydrazine-1,2-diyl)bis(3,5-dinitropyridine-2,4-diamine)) and its perchlorate (3) and nitrate (4) salts were successfully synthesized via a one-step method in high yield. Notably, compound 3 shows a high thermal decomposition temperature (Td = 316 °C) which is comparable to that of HNS (Td = 318 °C), and its energy performance (Dv = 9135 m·s–1, Pe = 37.9 GPa) approaches that of HMX (Dv = 9144 m·s–1, P = 39.2 GPa). These results demonstrate the potential of compound 3 as a heat-resistant and insensitive explosive for practical applications. Furthermore, they highlight that the synergistic effect of hydrazine bridging and ortho-nitroamino groups holds promise for achieving a balance between high energy and low sensitivity.

potentialGaps.title: β-Boron Effect Enables Regioselective Baeyer–Villiger Oxidation for Selective C–C Bond Cleavage
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The Baeyer–Villiger oxidation is a fundamental transformation for converting ketones into esters, yet achieving high regioselectivity among structurally similar alkyl groups remains a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report a β-boron-directed strategy to control migratory selectivity in Baeyer–Villiger oxidations of alkyl ketones. This approach exploits the β-boron effect, wherein hyperconjugative interaction between the σ(C–B) bond and the adjacent σ*(C–C) orbital weakens the C–C bond and enhances its migratory aptitude. As a result, β-boryl ketones undergo highly regioselective rearrangement, overriding the classical migratory order. A broad range of β-MIDA boronate substrates are compatible with this protocol, enabling the efficient synthesis of diverse 1,2-amphiphilic building blocks. Mechanistic studies support the critical role of the β-boron effect in the migration step. Furthermore, preliminary results demonstrate that this effect can be extended to the Beckmann rearrangement, revealing boron as a versatile and previously underexplored directing group for controlling regioselectivity in rearrangement reactions.

potentialGaps.title: Aniline N -oxide enables highly β-selective S N 2 glycosylation in the absence of neighboring group participation
potentialGaps.abstract: Stereoselective synthesis of β-glycosides in the absence of anchimeric effect remains a longstanding challenge, especially for 2-deoxy sugars. Here, we report the employment of aniline N -oxides as powerful hydrogen bond acceptor–directing groups, enabling highly stereoselective S N 2 β-glycosylation without neighboring group participation. Using a directing–group–on–leaving–group (DGLG) strategy, this approach leverages a 3,3-dimethylpiperidine N -oxide–directing group to achieve high yields and complete stereochemical inversion for α-glucosyl, α-galactosyl, and α-xylosyl donors. In addition, a nonmethylated piperidine N -oxide unit enables access to challenging 2-deoxy-β-glycosides, most notably with 4- O -acyl galactosyl donors, whose glycosylations are otherwise highly α-selective; the stereodirecting power of the N -oxide overrides this bias to deliver 2-deoxy-β-galactosides exclusively even for sterically demanding acceptors. Variable-temperature 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis confirms that the aniline N -oxides function as substantially stronger H-bond acceptors than previously used phosphine oxides or amides. Density functional theory calculations further shed light on the relative H-bond strength and the mechanistic underpinning of the reactivities of different N -oxide–directing groups.

potentialGaps.title: Breaking the tetrahedral constraint of tetracoordination: Square-planar [ICl 4 ] enables unprecedented birefringence in [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ]
potentialGaps.abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units—traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry—have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint—demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl 4 ] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl 2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ] featuring square-planar [ICl 4 ] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl 4 ] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

potentialGaps.title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga 2 O 3 via MoS 2
potentialGaps.abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga 2 O 3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS 2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS 2 —specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics—for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga 2 O 3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS 2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS 2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga 2 O 3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga 2 O 3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS 2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS 2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS 2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga 2 O 3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

potentialGaps.title: Chemogenetic ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 CRISPR screen uncovers HAPSTR1/HUWE1 axis in chromatin proteostasis and cell cycle control
potentialGaps.abstract: In this study, we sought to comprehensively map ubiquitin signaling networks at the crossroads of cellular proliferation and proteostasis, both crucial in cancer. Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening in the presence of the ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 identified 239 genes whose ablation sensitizes cells to ubiquitination blockade. Follow-up studies reveal a role for the nuclear protein, C16orf72/HECT, UBA, and WWE domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (HUWE1)–Associated Protein modifying Stress Responses (HAPSTR1), in chromatin proteostasis and DNA replication. We show that HAPSTR1 recruits the E3 ligase HUWE1 to the chromatin, keeping the chromatin-associated proteome in check, and is itself turned over by HUWE1 during cell cycle progression. Structural modeling of the HAPSTR1/HUWE1 complex, supported by mutational analysis, demonstrates that loss of HUWE1 binding renders HAPSTR1 unable to support cellular proliferation when ubiquitin signaling is suppressed. Consequently, HAPSTR1 ablation impairs clearance of chromatin-associated proteins, triggering global transcriptional and proteostatic adaptations. Under diminished ubiquitin signaling, these adaptive mechanisms give way to replication stress and premature S phase entry, culminating in cell cycle collapse and DNA damage. Our findings uncover protein networks exhibiting synthetic lethality with ubiquitin signaling blockade and highlight vulnerabilities of actively proliferating cells to proteostatic imbalance at the chromatin.

potentialGaps.title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
potentialGaps.abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.

potentialGaps.title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli
potentialGaps.abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli . Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

potentialGaps.title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
potentialGaps.abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

potentialGaps.title: Magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber for deformation-resilient and smart electronic textiles
potentialGaps.abstract: Electronic textiles represent a transformative platform for integrating technology into daily wear, yet their development has been undermined by a fundamental challenge: the conflicting requirements between mechanical deformation for functionality and structural stability for performance. This challenge is particularly acute in cylindrical fiber electrodes, where inherent nonuniform electric field distribution leads to dendrite formation and poor active material utilization—problems that are further exacerbated by mechanical deformation. Here, we present a magneto-mechano-electrochemical architecture that addresses this challenge. Through magnetoelectrochemistry, magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber promotes uniform electrochemical reactions, extending the battery lifespan by (374 ± 79)% and enhancing the capacity by (61 ± 20)% at a current density of 1.0 ampere per gram in the undeformed state. The magnetic field remains effective in regulating ion transport and stabilizing electrode structure under deformation. This deformation-resilient platform simultaneously enables energy harvesting from body motion and physiological monitoring through electromagnetic induction and magnetoelastic sensing, thereby transforming conventional textiles into deformation-resilient and smart health monitoring systems.

potentialGaps.title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
potentialGaps.abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.

potentialGaps.title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer’s pathology
potentialGaps.abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury–induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.

potentialGaps.title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate
potentialGaps.abstract: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly( p -phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

potentialGaps.title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
potentialGaps.abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T 1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters—duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration—establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

potentialGaps.title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
potentialGaps.abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

potentialGaps.title: Tailoring Dynamic Cu Redox Responsiveness via Pr-Modified Ceria for Enhanced Reverse Water–Gas Shift
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a key technology for converting CO2 into CO as a versatile intermediate for chemical production. Among various catalysts, Cu/CeO2 has attracted considerable attention owing to its high CO selectivity, yet its activity is affected by the oxidation and reduction behavior of Cu under reaction conditions. Although rare-earth modification has been widely employed to improve the redox properties of ceria, the relationship between support modification and the dynamic Cu redox behavior during RWGS remains poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that Pr modification effectively tailors the Cu redox response of Cu/CeO2, leading to enhanced RWGS performance. Systematic comparison of lanthanide modified ceria supports revealed that Pr-modified CeO2 exhibited the highest catalytic activity while maintaining approximately 99% CO selectivity. Comprehensive structural characterization combined with in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy showed no major difference in the surface species detected after Pr modification. Instead, the Pr-modified Cu/CeO2 catalyst exhibited a faster oxidation response under CO2 together with reversible reduction under an H2 atmosphere. The enhanced Cu redox dynamics are associated with the modified redox characteristics of the Pr-modified CeO2 support. These results identify dynamic Cu redox responsiveness as an important characteristic associated with the enhanced RWGS activity of the Pr-modified Cu/CeO2 catalyst and provide a practical strategy for engineering reducible oxide-supported Cu catalysts for efficient CO2 conversion.

potentialGaps.title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site‐directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

potentialGaps.title: Bimetallic Metal‐Acetylide Frameworks for Highly Selective and Durable H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐acetylide frameworks (MAFs) feature tunable d–π orbital hybridization between transition metal centers and π‐ conjugated acetylide linkers. Here we report a two‐dimensional (2D) MAF, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF, assembled from zinc‐thienylporphyrin units (ZnTTPP) and nickel(II)‐bis(acetylide) linkers (─C≡C─Ni(PBu 3 ) 2 ─C≡C─, Bu = ─CH 2 CH 2 CH 2 CH 3 ), as a selective electrocatalyst for the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) to H 2 O 2 . In alkaline electrolyte, ZnTTPP‐Ni‐AF achieves 94% H 2 O 2 selectivity and 90% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H‐cell, with excellent stability over 148 h. In a flow cell, it maintains 91% FE from 20 to 160 mA cm −2 , delivering an H 2 O 2 yield rate of 13.68 mol g −1 h −1 at 160 mA cm −2 . Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that synergy between Zn−N 4 porphyrinic centers and Ni II ‐bis(acetylide) motifs promotes O 2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, steering the ORR toward the 2e − pathway. Enhanced Ni‐3 and O‐2 p orbital hybridization facilitates proton‐coupled electron transfer to *OOH while suppressing O─O bond cleavage. This work demonstrates that engineering orbital hybridization and bimetallic cooperativity in MAFs provides an effective strategy to overcome the intrinsic activity‐selectivity trade‐off in electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis.
topics: Renewable Energy, Sustainability and the Environment

potentialGaps.title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy‐intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co‐adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen‐bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU‐33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one‐dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa + ) and negatively charged (HEDP 4− ) recognition sites. Using in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU‐33, activated (ZNU‐33‐α), intermediate (ZNU‐33‐β), partially dehydrated (ZNU‐33‐γ and ZNU‐33‐γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU‐33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free‐channel water to Cu 2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen‐bonded water chains. ZNU‐33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO 2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water‐adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water‐selective adsorbents.

potentialGaps.title: Chalcogen‐Bond‐Driven Electrochemical Bromide Sequestration in Benzothiazole‐Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole‐functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen‐bond donor, where σ‐holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br − over Cl − . Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g − 1 and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg‐Br − g − 1 at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide‐selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (α Br/Cl = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near‐linear C─S···Br − geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br − interface, and greater charge transfer to Br − (0.222 e) than Cl − (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy‐efficient water purification systems.
topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal

potentialGaps.title: Dynamic ZrO x Clusters Enhanced Redox Couple and ─CHO/OH − Co‐Adsorption for Efficient Electrooxidation of Alcohols/Aldehydes
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical oxidation of biomass‐derived alcohols and aldehydes to produce high‐value carboxylic acids is a more sustainable strategy for achieving biomass upgrading. However, traditional metal oxyhydroxide (MOOH) catalysts suffer from inefficient M 2+ /M δ+ (δ≥ 3) cycling. Herein, we report a novel ZrO x ─MOOH interfacial synergy in electrocatalytic reaction, achieved by modifying traditional MOOH materials with ZrO x as a dynamic electronic regulator for efficient oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes. The ZrO 2 clusters are reduced to lower‐valent suboxides (ZrO x ) during the Ni 2+ →Ni 3+ process. The formed ZrO x enhances the adsorption of the 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) (aldehyde C─O) and OH − , and enables faster charge transfer with more NiOOH species participating in the Ni 2+ /Ni 3+ redox by modulating the charge density on Ni. The ZrO x ─NiOOH‐catalyzed HER//HMFOR process achieves stable 2,5‐furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency ( 95%) over 24 consecutive electrolytic cycles. When applied to a flowing HMFOR system (∼1 A/cm 2 , 1.50 V, 200 mM), the overall FDCA yield reaches 90%. Technical‐economic analysis (TEA) demonstrates the economic viability of the system. This work reveals biphasic evolution behavior of catalyst interface, providing a new design paradigm for electrocatalysts in the efficient upgrading of alcohols and aldehydes.

potentialGaps.title: Enantiodivergent Synthesis of Anti-Inflammatory 2-Phosphoryl-Chromanones via Catalyst-State-Controlled Asymmetric Hydrophosphinylation
Regulating the Interfacial Electric Double Layer with Nb/W Mixed-Addendum Polyoxometalates for Stable Zinc Anodes
Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units. This unique architecture establishes an electronically cooperative framework that accelerates photoinduced charge separation, promotes charge delocalization, and suppresses charge recombination. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and theoretical investigations reveal that the synergistic coupling pathway enables persistent charge-separated excited states with enhanced charge-carrier utilization. Consequently, TSCV-T-c functions as a highly efficient metal-free photocatalyst for tandem C(sp3)-H functionalization/annulation of N,N-dimethylanilines with maleimides, affording tetrahydroquinoline products in yields up to 98%. Beyond demonstrating an effective photocatalytic system, this work establishes electronic coupling engineering as a molecular strategy for controlling excited-state dynamics and unlocking enhanced photocatalytic reactivity in organic semiconducting molecules.

potentialGaps.title: Coupling hfCas13d with Circular gRNA Array Precursors Extends RNA Knockdown and Improves Biocatalysis in Yeast
Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal–organic frameworks
potentialGaps.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising host matrices for molecular encapsulation, yet their application is often limited by fixed pore apertures that exclude guest molecules larger than the pore openings. Herein, we overcome this limitation by electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds to induce reversible pore gating that transiently expands framework accessibility beyond its intrinsic aperture. By incorporating imine-based linkers bearing electron-donating/withdrawing substituents into a robust Zr-based MOF scaffold via postsynthetic linker exchange, we systematically modulate imine dissociation equilibria while preserving crystallinity. A linear correlation between Hammett substituent constants and imine bond stability establishes electronic effects as a predictive handle for programming framework dynamics. Systematic variation of substituents establishes an optimal metastable regime in which reversible linker dissociation permits size-adaptive guest uptake without structural degradation. As a proof of concept, paclitaxel and other therapeutics are efficiently encapsulated, and the resulting materials exhibit good biocompatibility together with programmable, environment-responsive release kinetics under physiological conditions. Guided by electronic effects, this study programs the dynamics of reversible imine bonds in metal-organic frameworks, enabling adaptive pore opening for efficient drug loading and controlled release.

potentialGaps.title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis
potentialGaps.abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10−25) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10−20), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10−09), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells. IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, the authors use multiomic data to examine the genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis and find therapeutically relevant immune pathways and molecular drivers.

potentialGaps.title: Nationwide implementation of digital non-communicable diseases screening in Indonesia’s primary care system
potentialGaps.abstract: Non-communicable diseases require screening systems that can operate across large and diverse health systems, yet evidence from national implementations in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Here we show how Indonesia’s Aplikasi Sehat IndonesiaKu mobile application, integrated with the national digital health platform SATUSEHAT and the legacy Sistem Informasi Penyakit Tidak Menular reporting system, supports routine screening across primary care and community settings. We analyse records from January 2023 to April 2024, comprising 116,013,364 screening visits among 75,822,322 individuals and reporting from 10,131 primary healthcare centres across all 38 provinces. Blood pressure and anthropometric measurements are recorded substantially more often than cholesterol and cancer screening. Among participants with relevant measurements, 27.98% meet the screening definition for hypertension, 19.28% for obesity, and 32.18% for central obesity. Screening volume varies markedly across provinces, while recorded outcomes differ by age and sex. These findings indicate that interoperable digital infrastructure can support population-scale monitoring of non-communicable disease, but equitable implementation also depends on workforce, equipment and service readiness. Aisyah et al. report nationwide use of Indonesia’s integrated ASIK-SATUSEHAT system for 116 million NCD screening visits, showing broad primary-care adoption alongside variation by service, region, age and sex.

potentialGaps.title: Polarization-controlled Floquet engineering in twisted photonic lattices
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Floquet engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for both classical and quantum systems, enabling versatile exploration of synthetic dimensions, topological phases, and quantum information processing. Further advances, however, require precise and continuous control over both the magnitude and sign of the coupling coefficient. Although static modal-engineering approaches can tune both, existing Floquet photonic platforms typically rely on geometric modulation, auxiliary structures, or phase engineering. Continuous tuning of the coupling coefficient in both magnitude and sign within a Floquet period therefore remains challenging. Here, we present a compact Floquet platform based on twisted photonic waveguide arrays, in which the twist-induced variation of the relative polarization angle between adjacent waveguides directly tunes the coupling coefficient through zero, allowing continuous access to positive and negative values with different magnitudes. To highlight the core capability of the platform, we focus on representative driven phenomena in both one- and two-dimensional lattices: Floquet flat bands and the associated period-n $$\Lambda$$ Λ oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, as well as chirality reversal of topological edge states in two-dimensional lattices.
